## About me

I am a scientific computing and data-science professional with a Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, PMP certification, and a multidisciplinary background in computational biology, toxicology, cheminformatics, and AI/ML for life sciences. My work spans scientific workflow development, high-performance computing, molecular modeling, data-centric analysis, and prototype AI systems for drug safety and discovery.

In my recent role at [BHSAI / Henry M. Jackson Foundation](https://bhsai.org/), I developed end-to-end computational toxicology workflows for translational research across DoD-, DTRA-, NIH-, and AFRL-funded programs. My contributions included:

- **Scientific workflow delivery:** Translating scientific questions into reproducible analytical plans, resource-aware computational pipelines, validation strategies, and decision-ready outputs for cross-functional teams.
- **ML-enabled neurotoxicity profiling:** Building predictive models for neurotoxicity-relevant targets, integrating curated bioactivity data, molecular descriptors, and class-imbalance-aware ML workflows.
- **AI-enabled drug safety and discovery prototyping:** Developing Python-based workflow prototypes using classical ML, DNNs, GNNs, transformer models, and agentic AI approaches for prioritization and compound intelligence.
- **MEA and dose-response analysis:** Analyzing 200+ chemicals with high-dimensional Multi-Electrode Array (MEA) data, applying quality review and concentration-response modeling to identify neurotoxic liabilities.
- **Toxicogenomics and biomarker discovery:** Building reusable RNA-Seq pipelines for rat, guinea pig, and human hepatocyte studies to detect injury-associated biomarkers and support in vitro–in vivo interpretation.
- **Integrative safety science:** Connecting genomics, bioinformatics, toxicology, chemistry, and ADMET evidence to improve mechanistic understanding of chemical impact on human health.

Earlier, I was a postdoctoral researcher at [Dr. MacKerell's CADD Center](https://mackerell.umaryland.edu/), University of Maryland, where I developed the [SILCS](https://silcsbio.com/) computational drug discovery framework, including water-network modeling and binding-affinity workflows for small-molecule design and safety profiling.

I work effectively across biology, toxicology, chemistry, software engineering, and IT teams to turn complex datasets and molecular evidence into actionable insight. I am especially interested in computational safety science, new approach methodologies (NAMs), and AI-assisted scientific workflows that improve translational decision-making.

**I'm currently open to new opportunities** in scientific computing, computational toxicology, drug screening & discovery, or AI/ML for life sciences. [Get in touch →](mailto:hgchemical@gmail.com)
